Kelly / Mark — thanks for the note and the redlines. Appreciate the clarity.

Quick commercial reply while I coordinate with Legal/Contracts: our typical approach for customers of this size is a two-tiered "waterfall" that balances per-incident exposure with an annual aggregate bucket. The idea is to limit extreme single-event exposure while keeping overall annual risk aligned to actual spend. Roughly: 

- Per-incident cap: up to 3x the monthly invoice (or a fixed floor)
- Annual cap (resetting): greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $1,000,000

We also carve out (i) breach of confidentiality/customer data (we treat data breaches differently and often accept higher exposure), (ii) IP indemnity claims, and (iii) gross negligence/willful misconduct. Consequential damages remain excluded.

If you prefer a multiple-of-fees approach for both per-incident and annual buckets we can propose language for Legal to review. I'll loop in Legal for a formal redline and try to give you an option set (multiple-of-fees vs fixed-dollar floor) by EOD tomorrow.

—Priyom
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: Stately — cap proposal options and ask

Team — inbound from Stately (attached). They want "annual fees paid" as a cap or a multiple-of-fees fallback. Commercial wants to avoid an unconstrained contract term cap (i.e., total fees over the full term) because it inflates exposure if the contract runs long.

My proposed options to present to the customer: 
1) Waterfall A (preferred): Per-incident = max(3x monthly invoice, $250k); Annual aggregate = greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months, or (ii) $1,000,000. Resets every 12 months.
2) Waterfall B (legal-friendly): Per-incident = 3x monthly invoice; Annual aggregate = 3x average monthly invoice x 12 (i.e., 36x monthly) with a contract-term cap equal to 3x annual — simpler math for auditors.
3) Fixed-floor approach: Annual aggregate = greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $3,000,000 (fixed dollar).

Questions for Legal: 
- Acceptable carve-outs (we currently carve out IP indemnity, breach of confidentiality, and willful misconduct).
- Can we add an insurance-offset clause (liability reduced by amounts recoverable from insurance)?
- Preference between multiple-of-fees (dynamic) vs fixed-dollar floor (predictable).

Can you please provide redline language and a short rationale for customer-facing negotiation by EOD? Need to share consolidated counter by 5pm PST.

Thanks,
—Priyom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 10:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Stately — cap proposal options and ask

Priyom — quick legal read and suggested customer-facing language below. High level: Legal is comfortable with a multiple-of-fees structure tied to prior 12 months because it scales with customer's spend and is easier to justify to procurement. Recommend keeping a fixed-dollar floor to avoid very small caps for new customers. Also recommend explicitly enumerating carve-outs.

Suggested redline (customer-facing): 
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the aggregate liability of Redwood Inference for claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid to Redwood under this Agreement during the twelve (12) month period preceding the event giving rise to liability and (b) One Million United States Dollars (US$1,000,000). Notwithstanding the foregoing, the foregoing limitation shall not apply to liability arising from (i) Redwood's breach of its confidentiality obligations with respect to Customer Data, (ii) Redwood's indemnification obligations for third-party intellectual property infringement claims, and (iii) gross negligence or willful misconduct. For the avoidance of doubt, per-incident liability shall not exceed Three Times (3x) the Customer's then-current monthly recurring fees, subject to the aggregate annual cap above."

Notes: 
- Insurance-offset: we can include language that any recovery from insurance is credited, subject to the customer's duty to mitigate and cooperate with claims handling. That helps limit double recoveries.
- Consequential damages: keep exclusion in place; carve-outs above remain.
- If customer insists on term-based (total fees for full term) we should push back; explain commercial rationale (inflated cap for long terms).

I can produce a tracked-change MS Word redline if you want.

—Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
